findings.finding: Enagás paid EUR573m on 30 July to close the 31.5% Teréga stake, after H1 net debt of EUR2,305m and before the 2 July supplementary dividend. Q3 net debt should therefore print near EUR2.9-3.0bn, and the ~EUR2.4bn year-end target, set before the deal, will probably be restated. The money buys a regulated French TSO stake that broker Renta 4 calls >5% accretive to net profit and that the company says strengthens the dividend policy.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not observed on a results day. Enagás's results-day moves on real dates have a median of 0.82% across 24 prints, and its Q3 prints were +0.64, -0.08, +2.14, +1.70, -0.60 and +0.21 (Yahoo bars on issuer calendar dates).
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced. The amount and the closing were filed as OIR in July, and any analyst can add EUR573m to the debt. What is still unknown is whether the company re-bases the net-debt target and FFO/net debt (>15% for BBB+) explicitly. If the market had worried about leverage, the stock would have fallen around 30 July. Instead it slid gently from 17.45 to 16.9 with the sector, nothing an event drove.
findings.independence: Renta 4, 21 Apr 2026: deal accretion >5% to net profit and pressure on the balance sheet. https://www.r4.com/articulos-y-analisis/valores/enagas-1t26-reducimos-a-mantener-anuncian-compra-de-participacion-en-uno-de-los-operadores-del-sistema-frances-terega

findings.finding: The CNMC approved the final 2027-2032 gas transport and regasification circulars on 18 Sept 2026 (TRF 6.46%, in force 1 Oct). Brokers put the revenue uplift against 2026 at about EUR75-80m a year. The Q3 release is the first results document after approval and may carry Enagás's own 2027 regulated-revenue figure, although the full strategic plan is guided to H1 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The draft framework on 27 Mar 2026 moved the stock +16.96% (Yahoo bars). The final approval on 18 Sep 2026 moved it -0.12%, so the framework news was priced at the draft.
findings.original_quote: se fija una tasa de retribución financiera del 6,46 % (a financial return rate of 6.46% is set); Las Circulares entrarán en vigor el 1 de octubre de 2026 (the circulars will enter into force on 1 October 2026)
findings.why_not_priced: The framework itself is priced: the stock did not move on final approval. What is not priced is the company's own number, which no document has given yet. Brokers disagree (Renta 4 TP 20.30 Buy on 28 Sep, Morgan Stanley 16.00 Sell on 11 Sep), so a company figure could settle the dispersion. Most of this moves the stock only if the company gives the figure, and the H1 2027 strategic plan timing makes that uncertain.

language_note: The CNMC press note (Spanish) is the primary source for the final 6.46% rate and the 1 Oct 2026 entry into force. English coverage carried it only second-hand through German and English broker wires.

The Spanish press (El Debate, El Español) carried the company's statement that H1 EBITDA is coherent with the EUR620m target because cost-related revenues fall in H2, and that Teréga's remaining approvals were expected in Q3. The English Quartr summary carried only the reaffirmed targets.
The issuer's own OIR list, published in English and Spanish, gave the Teréga closing date and the bmo timing, so it was not Spanish-only.
lessons_applied: 'Too small about the move; let reaction history move p_up, not abs_move': abs_move_pct raised from 1.6 to 2.0. It is still below the 2.3% European reiterated-guide median because of this name's 15% realised vol and its 0.82% observed median over 24 real results days.
'Financing is a question': the Teréga debt finding moved from -0.2 to -0.1, because the money buys accretive regulated earnings and the debt step-up is mechanical.
'A number the market has already been told is worth 0': confirmed the in-guide 9M finding at 0.0. No change.
